desc: Implement an iterative segment tree with associative node combine `(total, pref, suff, best)`, a true empty identity (using `-inf` sentinels so all-negative arrays stay correct), and inclusive range-aggregate queries; explicitly design the merge formulas and empty-range behavior.
Build value -> sorted positions dict (hash map, since values are large) and compute the baseline no-operation answer from the segment-tree root's `best`.

For each distinct value x with freq[x] < n, walk its sorted positions, query each non-empty gap (before first, between consecutive, after last occurrence) and merge gap aggregates in order — relying on the gap-concatenation reduction that post-deletion subarrays are exactly concatenations of consecutive non-x gaps (partial at the ends); record the resulting aggregate's `best`.
Return the max of the baseline and every filtered aggregate's `best`, skipping values whose deletion empties the array.

Test against both provided examples plus edge cases: all-equal array, single element, all-negative array, consecutive duplicates, alternating values; run random brute-force comparison for small n; confirm O(n log n) time and O(n) memory.
